The BDS-PF provides annual statistics for 1978 to 2023 by patenting status and a series of firm and establishment characteristics including size, age, industry, and geography. pages.text: Business Dynamics Statistics of Single Unit Firms with Revenue (BDS-SU-REV) Business Dynamics Statistics of Single Unit Firms with Revenue (BDS-SU-REV) Skip Navigation Business Dynamics Statistics of Single Unit Firms with Revenue (BDS-SU-REV) September 2026 The Business Dynamics Statistics of Single Unit Firms with Revenue (BDS-SU-REV) is an experimental data product extending the set of statistics published by the Business Dynamics Statistics (BDS) program. The BDS-SU-REV provides year-over-year changes in employment, payroll, and revenue for each quarter of the year for businesses that operate in one location (single-units) and file their taxes under a single Employer Identification Number (EIN). This product relies on IRS annual tax filings to collect revenue information and IRS quarterly tax filings to collect employment and payroll information for the pay periods including March 12 th , June 12 th , September 12 th , and December 12 th . Year-over-year employment and payroll changes are calculated between the same point in year t and year t-1 (i.e., June 12 th year t-1 to June 12 th year t, etc.). Employment and payroll growth is labeled as job and pay creation respectively and employment and payroll decline as job and pay destruction. A novel innovation in the BDS-SU-REV is the incorporation of annual revenue data for single-establishment firms that consistently maintain positive employment levels each quarter. A positive annual growth in revenue is categorized as revenue creation, while negative growth is categorized as revenue destruction. Jump to: Data Definitions

pages.text: Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS) Data Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS) Data Skip Navigation Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS) Data July 13, 2026 The Business Trends and Outlook Survey provides high-frequency, nationally representative data on U.S. employer businesses. The survey provides local, state, and federal officials near real-time data for policy and decision-making including after natural disasters or during economic crises. The BTOS also provides insights into business recovery after these events. The BTOS sample consists of approximately 1.2 million businesses split into six panels (approximately 200,000 cases per panel). Businesses in each panel are asked to report once every 12 weeks over the course of one year. Data collection occurs every two weeks. The BTOS is comprised of a set of core questions and supplemental content, which is added as needed. The BTOS collects information on a broad range of business conditions. Topics include current performance, changes in revenue, employment, hours worked, demand, and prices. For most concepts, businesses are asked about the previous two weeks and for a 6-month outlook. Data collected from September 11, 2023 to present include all employer businesses (single location and multi-location) in the U.S. economy, excluding farms. BTOS data are released every two weeks and are available by 2022 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) sector, by state and for the 25 most populous Metropolitan Statistical Areas. pages.description: Peter Bradshaw: Reasonably amusing, with 2-D acting and writing, and Day-Glo pink and blue colour schemes.
pages.text: But I'm a Cheerleader | Movies | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Movies This article is more than 25 years old Review But I'm a Cheerleader This article is more than 25 years old Peter Bradshaw Thu 12 Apr 2001 21.12 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google D irector and co-writer Jamie Babbit makes her feature debut with this satire of America's creepy Christian "sexual reorientation" camps, where confused teens are sent so that their nascent gayness can be deprogrammed out of them. Natasha Lyonne plays Megan, a cheerleader who hugs her fellow pom-pom-botherers inappropriately and hates making out with her jock boyfriend. He and Megan's family arrange an "intervention" where she is confronted with her shameful tendencies and sent to the True Directions camp, run by two smug tyrants in Straight Is Great T-shirts, played by Cathy Moriarty and RuPaul (here out of drag), clearly repressed gays themselves. Once there, Megan falls for a girl with the interesting name of Graham, played by Clea DuVall. As in all therapy boot-camp movies - such as Girl, Interrupted, in which DuVall had a role - there has to be a wild child with whom the heroine makes a connection. This is Graham's role. It's reasonably amusing, with 2-D acting and writing, and Day-Glo pink and blue colour schemes. But it could have been funnier, and I would have preferred to know more in documentary terms about the actual reality of these terrible camps, rather than sit through this heavy-handed and oddly lenient comedy. Then read on. Which train ticket is the best choice for me? As a general rule, the earlier you can buy a ticket, the better the price you can get. If you know the date and time you wish to travel, then an Advance ticket will be suitable. For more flexibility, Off-Peak and Super Off-Peak tickets and Anytime tickets will be a better option, as you are not limited to a specific date or train. For more information about getting the most affordable ticket for your journey, see below. Advance tickets These must be bought in advance and are only valid on the date and train specified. They are sold in limited numbers, subject to availability and on a first come, first served basis. You can usually buy an Advance ticket up to 12 weeks ahead of travel, and they are still available until the day of travel on many routes – sometimes up to 10 minutes before departure. They offer a great deal if you know exactly when you want to travel. Find out more about Advance tickets . Off-Peak and Super Off-Peak tickets These good value tickets can be bought at any time and allow you to travel on any permitted train during off-peak hours. If an Off-Peak or Super Off-Peak ticket is available for your journey, journey planners will make them available to purchase. In general, Off-Peak hours begin at 09:30 from Monday to Friday in cities and large towns, and at 09:00 everywhere else.

pages.description: Whether it’s a short hop across the Channel or an overland expedition to the furthest reaches of Europe, some of the richest travel experiences happen when you skip the flight.
pages.text: By Land and Sea—17 European Trips From London | National Geographic By Oliver Smith Published October 24, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Today, it’s easier to travel further and faster around Europe than ever before — to board a flight and effectively parachute yourself into a new destination. But by travelling overland, be it by ferry, train or car, on a bike or on foot, you’re able to observe the slow, subtle changes at ground level with every accumulated mile. Overland travel by rail is also easier than it’s ever been, thanks to an ever-expanding network of high-speed and sleeper trains across Europe. You might board a morning Eurostar at London St Pancras International and that same day be joining a midnight crawl of Madrid’s tapas bars or standing beneath Milan’s hulking Duomo as stars twinkle above its white marble facade. Ferries, too, offer perspectives unfamiliar to those at the cruising altitude of an airliner, whether that’s witnessing the green coast of northern Spain unravelling out of the blue horizons of Biscay or seeing Icelandic volcanoes peek over grey North Atlantic waves. Unless otherwise noted, the Court generally hears two, one-hour oral arguments, with attorneys for each side of a case given 30 minutes to make a presentation to the Court and answer questions posed by the Justices. These sessions are open to the public. Non-argument Days: The Court convenes for a session in the Courtroom at 10 a.m. The session begins with the announcement of opinions - decisions in argued cases - followed by the swearing in of new members to the Bar of the Supreme Court. These sessions, which typically last 15-30 minutes, are open to the public. Conference Days: The Justices meet in a private conference to discuss cases argued earlier that week. The Justices also discuss and vote on petitions for review. The building is open to the public but the Justices do not take the Bench. Holiday: The Court is closed on federal holidays. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/calibration-services Standards Calibration services Sign Up to Get NIST News GovDelivery Purchase calibrations Learn more about calibrations NIST on a Chip If you need to measure something, NIST is the go-to place for help. And NIST is also the place to go if you need to calibrate your measuring equipment. In our everyday lives, calibrations are often the little adjustments you may make, for example to make sure the colors of your computer monitor or television are accurate, so it will show photos or videos the way that a filmmaker or photographer intended. But for a scientific measurement laboratory such as NIST, calibrations are a bit different. NIST calibrations determine a relationship between the measurement standard (like the Kibble balance) and that instrument or object (such as a cylindrical metal kilogram mass). By using a world-class reference such as the Kibble balance, calibrations make it possible for a piece of measuring equipment to make the most accurate measurement it can. From MRIs to lasers, NIST's calibration services are part of many aspects of everyday life. While many are familiar with the Oregon Trail, the California Trail is equally legendary, filled with stories of hope, hardships, and transformation. This historic route stretched thousands of miles across the West, turning travelers’ dreams and Native American ways of life into destinies marked by both gain and loss. Between 1841 and 1869, thousands of pioneers traveled nearly 2,000 miles from the Missouri River to the Sierra Nevada Mountains and beyond. Driven by hopes of fertile land, religious freedom, and gold, their journey was far from easy. Along the way, they faced disease, conflict, and dangerous terrain, including the infamous Donner Party disaster. Despite these hardships, people kept coming, lured by the promise of prosperity and adventure. Visit the California Trail Interpretive Center in Elko, Nevada, to explore the people and stories behind this epic journey. pages.description: Driven from the state generations ago, the predators are staging a comeback—and sparking a new fight over livelihood, identity, and the meaning of the wild.
pages.text: California's Wolves Have Returned After a Century. But at What Cost? | National Geographic Premium ANIMALS California's Wolves Have Returned After a Century. But at What Cost? Driven from the state generations ago, the predators are staging a comeback—and sparking a new fight over livelihood, identity, and the meaning of the wild. Across the pastures of Northern California, more than 200,000 cattle are under threat as wolves return to their former range. Ranch hand Sam Harper discovers a dead calf near the city of Montague. By Nate Blakeslee Photographs by Aaron Huey Published November 3, 2026 Susan H ar t firs t no t iced the wolves one summer about six years back. They’d pop up in the evenings on the ridges of the ranch she runs with her husband, Blair, whose family has raised cattle near Montague, California, since 1852. The Harts are one of the oldest ranching families in Siskiyou County, an enormous, sparsely populated region of rugged mountains and pristine valleys near the Oregon border. The most frequent visitor Susan saw was a wolf with a distinctive light coat and an injured foreleg that spent a lot of time watching the herd. It was clearly too slow to catch a mule deer, the most common prey animal in the nearby mountains, and Susan was worried that it was just a matter of time before it became bold enough to attack one of her animals. That day came in the fall of 2021, when she and Blair awoke to find a bloodied calf with a huge portion of its hide torn away. The calf somehow survived, but the wolves, known as the Whaleback pack, struck again roughly a year later

The Scot, 37, needed an operation for an injury sustained repeatedly punching a drinks table on stage following his first-round exit at the PDC World Championships last December. And he made headlines during the summer after requiring medical attention during his World Matchplay encounter with Ross Smith, which he had to forfeit. His dizzy turn was put down to high blood pressure caused by dehydration. "I didn't know what it was, I looked at the board and I just felt like everything was spinning," Menzies told BBC Scotland. The site provides outdoor recreation opportunities in a non-motorized natural setting for 400,000 to 500,000 visitors annually. Research tracking thousands of adults found that staying fit lowered mortality and liver disease risk among drinkers—though rising alcohol use still took a toll. Emerging research suggests that people who meet physical activity guidelines tend to have lower mortality and liver disease risk than inactive drinkers. But exercise doesn’t erase alcohol’s harm—it may reduce risk, not remove it. Elizabeth Weinberg, The New York Times/Redux By Hannah Singleton Published February 27, 2026 Over the past year, public health messaging about alcohol has shifted sharply. For decades, many people clung to the idea that a nightly glass of red wine might protect the heart. Now, both the World Health Organization and the U.S. Surgeon General have taken firm stances: no amount of alcohol is risk-free. Yet alcohol remains deeply embedded in how we celebrate, socialize, and relax. Despite the risks, many people still feel it’s worth drinking at least occasionally. “The recent guidelines clearly say that if you avoid alcohol like 100 percent, that is the best for you,” says Javaid Nauman , a professor at the Institute of Public Health at the United Arab Emirates University. “But we know at human levels, I don't think that it will ever happen.” That reality has prompted a new question among researchers: Can exercise buffer some of alcohol’s long-term risks?
